Derive outcomes, comorbidities, and costs

Source: vignettes/articles/outcomes-and-costs.Rmd
outcomes-and-costs.Rmd
library(easyNIS)
library(dplyr)
library(srvyr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

The examples use invented data.

Add outcomes and score comorbidities

The NIS has no diagnosis-level present-on-admission fields (DXPOA). The default Elixhauser method assumes diagnoses were present on admission. That assumption differs from the AHRQ Refined method with known POA. Document it if you use these scores for risk adjustment.

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020))
outcomes <- nis |> nis_outcomes()
outcomes |> count(in_hospital_death) |> collect()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   in_hospital_death     n
#>   <lgl>             <dbl>
#> 1 FALSE               188
#> 2 TRUE                  4

DIED defines in-hospital death. DISPUNIFORM describes where the patient went at discharge. los_days comes from LOS. Keep all three source fields when calling nis_outcomes().

Install medicalcoder to run this Charlson example. Expect a warning about absent present-on-admission fields. The method assumes the diagnoses were present on admission.

scored <- outcomes |> nis_comorbidity(method = "charlson_quan2005")
#> Warning: No matching POA column for some diagnosis slots. Assuming present on admission.
#> ℹ POA-dependent scores may include conditions acquired in hospital.
scored |> count(cmrb_n) |> arrange(cmrb_n) |> collect()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   cmrb_n     n
#>    <int> <dbl>
#> 1      0    38
#> 2      1   154

Score before nis_design() while the diagnosis slots are available and DuckDB can still apply the mappings. Choose the method and code system for your study period. The bundled "elixhauser_ahrq2027" method has no medicalcoder dependency.

Set count_distinct = TRUE to add the integer column cmrb_n_distinct. The distinct count counts each condition represented by the output flags once. For example, the refined Elixhauser flag for hypertension with heart failure and severe renal failure represents three conditions, even when separate flags for those conditions are also true. Diabetes and other severity variants of the same condition share an ID. cmrb_n still reports the method’s own category count.

method <- "elixhauser_ahrq2027"
condition_map <- nis_comorbidity_condition_map(method)
condition_map |> filter(condition == "diabetes")
#>           output condition
#> 1   cmrb_diab_cx  diabetes
#> 2 cmrb_diab_uncx  diabetes

outcomes |>
  nis_comorbidity(method, count_distinct = TRUE, exclude_conditions = "diabetes") |>
  count(cmrb_n, cmrb_n_distinct) |>
  arrange(cmrb_n, cmrb_n_distinct) |>
  collect()
#> Warning: No matching POA column for some diagnosis slots. Assuming present on admission.
#> ℹ POA-dependent scores may include conditions acquired in hospital.
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   cmrb_n cmrb_n_distinct     n
#>    <int>           <int> <dbl>
#> 1      0               0    38
#> 2      1               0   108
#> 3      1               1    46

Use IDs from the map to exclude conditions that your analysis handles separately. The count uses the flags emitted by the chosen method and inherits their present-on-admission assumptions. Exclusions affect only the distinct count. A discharge without usable codes has a missing count, and a discharge with usable codes and no included conditions has a count of zero.

Estimate costs in a common dollar year 

charges <- outcomes |> select(YEAR, TOTCHG, CCR_NIS) |> collect()
costs <- nis_cost(charges, dollars = 2020)
nis_cost_provenance(costs)$multipliers
#>   year multiplier
#> 1 2019   1.012337
#> 2 2020   1.000000
costs |>
  summarise(mean_charge = mean(charges_adj), mean_cost = mean(cost_adj), .by = YEAR)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>    YEAR mean_charge mean_cost
#>   <int>       <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1  2019      15009.     4428.
#> 2  2020      14828.     4374.

Join the year-specific HCUP cost-to-charge ratio before estimating costs if the data lack CCR_NIS. charges_adj is the adjusted billed amount. cost_adj applies the hospital ratio to estimate costs. Missing or invalid ratios yield missing costs. CPI-U tracks general consumer price inflation. It does not track hospital-specific input prices. When comparing with a legacy result, check its charge field, CCR source, price index, and dollar year. Keep the provenance alongside both cost and charge results. The means here describe the invented sample. Use the survey design for national estimates. Years and coding eras

If nis_design() keeps both TOTCHG and CCR_NIS, it adds charges_adj and cost_adj in dollars of the latest included year by default. Use nis_cost() to set a common dollar year across separate analyses and retain the provenance with your results.
